utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, the transcript didn't quite catch their names. If you could just maybe spell them for us, if that wouldn't trouble you too much?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: The first one is Baxendale, which is B-a-x-e-n-d-a-l-e, and Coslett, which is C-o-s-s-l-e-t-t.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did they generate a report as well?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Why wouldn't they?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Again it's not standard practice to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you have any evidence in your file that you have here in The Hague that they actually conducted this peer review checking or analysis on each of the reports that you generated?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you share with us and we're hopefully getting that, with the Court's permission of course, not to be presumptuous, what's contained within your binder or file that you brought with you here today?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: My notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your handwritten notes?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Handwritten notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And what do they consist of?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: My handwritten notes, my analysis of the work, my tick sheets.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So it includes, not only your tick sheet, but the number of documents that you may have reviewed. It includes the specimens that you may have drawn out from those documents in order to make your comparative it analysis between the similarities and the differences from the various letters, if you will, that you analysed; correct?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, do you have a chart or do you remember if you drew a chart to determine how many similarities versus how many differences you noted in your analysis of any one of these reports?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Does that exist in your folder?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: As you sit here, do you know how many you used on the first report generated on the 16th of July, 2003, with Mr. Jokic?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: How many similarities?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: No, but then it's not done on a number basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What's it's done on?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: My evaluation of the significance of the similarities and the differences.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And that's contained in your notes as well; correct?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How many differences did you detect?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Same point.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Same answer?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We'll be looking forward to getting ahead today to discuss it. Looking at your July 16th, 2003 report, I have a couple of specific questions if you don't mind. And if I could direct your attention to page 3, paragraph 5.4. We're going to focus on the next page, which is page 4, although I think you need in order to keep it in proper context read the prior page, to yourself, of course. Whenever you're ready?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'd like to focus on the last five or so words of page 3 and going forward to page 4 without taking it out of context. You discuss in that paragraph the factors that have restricted your comparisons to some extent, and then you talk about there are some features of the questioned writing that cannot be matched in the specimen.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Which features were those?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Predominantly, as I showed on the chart, there were differences in, for example, the capital As, which were more split up in the questioned than in the specimen. And also, the "I" dots were much more pronounced.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And what do you call that as a documents examiner, diacritic? Is that what it is?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: It means an "I" dot.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And in fact, just so that I understand it better, is that the letter or small letter "I", some people merely impress the pen to create what's called the dot and some create what's known as a circle or diacritic over the small letter "I"; correct?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: I think if a dot, it would still be a diacritic, but some people do small dots, some people do more obviously circles.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, how many samples, specimen samples, from Mr. Jokic did you use in order to evaluate whether this difference in A or this diacritic with the circle over the "I" was found?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: I used his personal information form and also some pages from -- which I originally described as the operational diary, which I had been told were his specimen writing.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you have any doubt about that?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Only that I think it's actually the official notebook judging by the IRN numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, the ERN numbers --

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: ERN, right.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's okay. I'm confused a little bit about your answer.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Maybe because I just don't understand it. That's okay I'll try to maybe -- or you can help me understand it. You have the official notebook which has the 10 pages of ERN numbers that you highlight in most, if not all of your reports, that start with the number 0293-5743, and they conclude at 0293-5753; correct?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Why were you limited in evaluating merely those 10 pages of the notebook?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: That's what I was asked to look at.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know why?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know if you ever received a sample specimen from Mr. Jokic where he specifically at the request of the Prosecution handwrote out, I believe verbatim, those 10 pages?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: I did, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. So you took a specific specimen sample and compared it to the same 10 pages that we call the questioned sampling, if you will?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And when was that done?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: That was done and is detailed in my third report. So it will be January 2004.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So, let's take that one which was his personal sampling of all 10 of the ERN numbers that you were asked to evaluate and you started to tell me, and I apologise if I interrupted you, that you also had some independent sampling from Mr. Jokic which was such as an application you were starting to say or --

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: I had his personal information form.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. And what other documents did you have?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: I had pages from the IKM logbook.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And anything else?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, did you at any time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Ostojic. In total how many specimens, signatures and handwriting, let's keep them separately, of Dragan -- of Jokic did you have available for comparison purposes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had no signatures. I had his personal information form. I had three entries from the IKM logbook, and I had the sample writing that he provided on request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And according to acknowledged, accepted practices in your field of expertise, would such an amount of samples, specimens, be sufficient for comparative purposes or -- or would you normally require much more?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's difficult to give a definitive answer because a lot of that will depend on, for example, how distinctive the handwriting is and whether you get all the characters in the specimen writing that occur in the questions. In general, it would be sufficient. The problem was that the sample handwriting that he produced on request, while it was, as far as I recall, a writing out of what was the questioned writing, it was obviously produced in 2004, so was post-dated quite considerably the actual questioned writing. So obviously that has to be taken into account.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] The other question I had for you but more or less you have dealt with it. Back to you Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let's take the converse of that last statement --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sorry, I can never get it right. Let's take the converse of your statement just now. Because it happened so long ago, isn't it true that just by that very fact, that the likelihood that you were able to find any similarities would have decreased?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: No, because generally once you reach mature adulthood, your writing will stay reasonably constant over a long period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And you didn't find that as any impediment or a problem to compare it, even though it was eight or so years later compared to the actual notebook that you reviewed?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: The problem is it's taken in context with the other writing as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Who -- did you recommend to the Prosecution that they request that Mr. Jokic give a sampling of those 10 pages verbatim?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: I can't remember whether I requested it or if it came up in discussions.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, what other features in the questioned writings could not be matched? We covered of them, I think the letter "A" you said, and then also the diacritic or the circle over the small "I." What other --

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Those were the only two that were clear, not -- things that you couldn't match at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So in fact -- just so that I'm clear, those aren't just features that you found differences in, those are absolutely no match; correct?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: The diacritic was, yes. The match within the block capitals was closer in the sample handwriting than it had been in the writing that I took from the IKM logbook.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, if I could just direct your attention to the same report which is 16th of July, 2003, the last paragraph, paragraph 5.4 on page 4, I have a couple of questions about that. You start by saying: "I would add that because of the nature of the entries, and I just want to break it down; although, I don't want you to be misled, obviously you continue in your paragraph. What about the nature of the entries were you concerned about when you generated this report?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: That -- from looking at the book, the writing appears to be lots of the short entries rather than -- although it covers a number of pages, it doesn't look as though it's written all at one time period straight after the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. So in fact, as you suggest in your report, the writings may have been added at a later date; correct?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, what analysis, if any, did you do in order to determine whether or not any of the writings may have been added at a later date?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: It was more that things have been overwritten. If things have been overwritten since you can't date inks you can't tell at what date they've been added.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So you've done no analysis whatsoever; correct?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: No. Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, continuing on paragraph 5.4 of your report, you say something that I find at least personally curious. You state that if any small amount of writing was taken in isolation, then the strength of the evidence linking to Drago Nikolic would necessarily be reduced. What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: To be able to do a handwriting comparison, you need to have enough writing to be able to reach a conclusion. For example, if I only had one character, then I wouldn't be able to reach a conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I read this a little differently, with all due respect, and maybe we can -- you could help me probably that I was inaccurate but we'll see. When you say if any amount of writing was taken in isolation, would that mean, perhaps, that if we took only the absolute differences that you denote that's in the letter "A" and in the diacritic and if we were -- just to compare those two points, you would find that taking that in isolation would decrease the strength of evidence linking it to Dragan Jokic, would it not?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: It would, but that would be only if you took, for example, the "I" on its own out of context and out of the other characters within the word.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You mentioned today in your direct examination that on page 28, line 19, that Jokic wrote in a scribbled manner. I don't think you have it.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That was just for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Yes, all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's okay. That he wrote in a scribbled manner. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: As I said in my examination, people write differently on different occasions, so I had entries that were in the notebook and I had entries that were in the IKM logbook. The ones in the IKM logbook looked neater. They were more clearly formed characters. The ones that were questioned looked in essence like they're scribbled in the same way that when you fill in a form that you know somebody else has got to read and is important to you, you write slowly and neatly. When you're just making notes for yourself then you tend to write faster, especially if you're getting other information.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What are the other characteristics of writing other than being neat or scribbled. There's block writing; right?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Yes. There's block writing and lowercase writing.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What else?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, let's talk about each of those. You considered Mr. Jokic to have scribbled writing as opposed to neat writing; correct?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Scribbled writing within the notebook. It was more scribbled, but he has neat writing as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In the IKM book?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: But within the notebook itself during -- or based upon those 10 pages that you evaluated, you found that his writing was scribbled as opposed to neat; correct?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And would you find his writing to be in lowercase or in block form?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: A mix of both.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. And how -- did you do a comparison as to how many were in block form versus how many were in --

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: -- small? Why not?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Because you can't compare -- well, if you're talking about numbers how many were in block and how much there -- I don't know. If you're talking to did I compare the block with the lowercase, you can't compare block with lowercase.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Because they're different forms of the same character.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And -- pardon me.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, just for the record, I misspoke on page 52, line 17, and I apologise to Mr. Nikolic. And just so that I think it's clear that I'm referencing Dragan Jokic and it says Nikolic on the record, and I apologise to counsel and to their client.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We were talking about Dragan Jokic at that time, and we're still talking about Dragan Jokic?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, what I'd like to do is to go through some of your analysis, or actually I want to talk about your range of opinions first; I'm sorry. Do you know if these are the seven standard range of opinions that the European and other industrialised countries use for their document -- forensic document examiners?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: I would imagine probably not. They're not even the standard within the UK.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And who came up with these range of opinions?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: The organisation I work for.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The company that you work for; correct?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And why are they different from other companies and other countries or other standards that people see from time to time?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: They're different simply in the wording of them and some other organisations maybe have more conclusion scales. The use of a verbal scale starting with conclusive and inconclusive in the middle is standard.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And then if inconclusive is in the middle, what's below that?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: It's a mirror image.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: So you have the positive when you're saying somebody wrote it, and you're having the negative.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If we were to discuss these range of opinions, in my view based on how the forensic institute here in the Netherlands does it with the Ministry of Justice, would you use at any point the word certainty?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: I would say conclusive evidence, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And what would you say for inconclusive?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: I would say I couldn't say one way or the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to show you if I may the notebook which is 377. And my learned friend has the original and that might be helpful for Ms. Barr if she needs it. And I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is it available here?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And if we could put it on the ELMO or if the Court wishes we can place the page which is ERN number 0293-5752 on e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, I just want -- I don't want to have any tragedies happening. Is this the book which had one or two pages? I think that had a brown -- brown cover. I don't think it's this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, this isn't that the one that had the page about to fall out. That was the IKM book.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. So still handle it with extreme care, because these documents are very fragile having gone through a war.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Ms. Barr if you don't mind can we place that with the Court's permission on the ELMO so that we can see the original together?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: With the Court's permission if we could place the original on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: By all means.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, if you look at this document and you're welcome to look to your right, you can turn your chair or whatever, the bottom portion is obviously written in what kind of script?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: The page on the left?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: 027935752, the page on the left, correct.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: It's written in lowercase writing.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And is it done in print form or is it a different form?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: I would say it's in cursive handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And where does it start, if you will, to become a cursive in lowercase?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: After the words, "126 Pozedina".

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, if we focus on the top portion you would agree with me that that's written in what type of -- is it cursive or how?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: The writing above the number?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Again, it has obviously block capital writing and lowercase writing that is more script.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know why there's a distinction or a difference there?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you find that by way of an example anywhere else in the pages or books including notebook, logbook, and IKM that you reviewed?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Did I find what, sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: An inconsistency of purportedly the same writer having written on the same page differently?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: There are other ones within here, where he writes. In essence that was my point about the entries made at different times, because you've got the different styles of writing.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: But do you notice, ma'am, in the top portion of that document that there is this diacritic over the letter I that you're never able to match with any other writing from Mr. Jokic; correct?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: But don't you see a diacritic over another letter there?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: The "J".

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The "J". Now, did you see that there's a similarity or a difference in that letter as well?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: To each other or to Mr. Jokic's writing?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, obviously to Mr. Jokic's writing.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Again, it's a diacritic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, what I'm looking for is to get your entire opinion, and I thought I understood it, and you said that the differences that you found that you were unable to match were limited to two, the "A" and also the diacritic over the letter "I"; correct?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: I possibly misled you. I think I said in my original report the diacritic for which I would be meaning over other characters as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, how many other characters would the diacritic appear on?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: The "J" and the "I", plus there are also other marks on there. For example --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You're flipping the pages so we can keep up?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's okay.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: For example, on the line below, five points out there are -- there are additional marks, for example, there that occur throughout this writing that don't occur in the specimen writing.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And thank you for that. And what other differences do you note?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Those were the differences.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Was the writing above the 126 in the same ink pen as the writing below the 126?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: I didn't do an examination. There's nothing to indicate it's not, there.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you think it would be beneficial or helpful given that there's differences - one's cursive, one's not; one is in black letters, the other part is not - to do such an evaluation.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: No, because it still fits in within the entirety of the writing that I'm looking at within there.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How long would it have taken you to do such an analysis or evaluation, if I may ask?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: The actual analysis itself of -- of that one entry would not have taken very long, but then I would have had to do it for every single entry within that, which would have taken -- well, then -- then you get to the point of at what point do I stop doing it? So if I had to do it for every single word to indicate that it was the same pen, then I have no idea how long that would take.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you evaluate the letter "B", for example, with respect to Mr. Jokic's handwriting?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: I would imagine so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. And what were your conclusions?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Without my notes, I couldn't tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know if, as we're looking on this exhibit here of 0293-5752, do you see the way in the first line how the letter "B" is written?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you find that letter "B" written as it's written there in any of Mr. Jokic's sampling -- sampler documents such as that which he provided you where he copied verbatim these 10 pages that you analysed or any of his application or other forms that you may have reviewed?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: I honestly don't know without recourse to my notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, that -- can you look here if he wrote anywhere another letter "B" on the page before, maybe if we take a look at 0293-5751? On that in the middle of the page the "B" is written almost, although I'm not a document handwriting examiner, it looks similar right in the middle of the page, does it not, where it says 155?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, right below that there's another word that's written, "Badem". Do you think that that's the same "B" or you can't really tell right here on the spot in court?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: It looks similar.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. What would you do to evaluate those two Bs? What's the methodology that you would utilise?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: I would look to see that they're the same construction and roughly the same proportions.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How would you go about doing it?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Using a microscope or in that case -- yeah, using a hand lens.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: But is it safe to say, ma'am, that in your notes that are -- not your office but the Office of the Prosecution somewhere, that you have this analysis with respect to the letter "B" as well; correct?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: I would imagine so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Going back to 0293-5752. Sorry. Do you -- can you tell by looking at this without the use of the electrostatic apparatus that you talks about and the ultra-red video equipment, can you see if this was written after or before the material that's provided below it?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Neither of those two bits of equipment would allow you to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What equipment would?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: There is no equipment that would.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What about the indent impressions that you talked about? Wouldn't you be able to analyse the original document and detect by looking at how it was indented on the previous, prior pages whether or not it was a late add-on or an addition at some time later?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: It's a possibility dependent on whether -- how many intersections you would get between the -- that writing and the writing underneath.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you perform any such analysis or evaluation?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Again, I wasn't asked to, and it wouldn't be standard practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: But given that you knew that the dates were written in by someone other than Mr. Jokic, did that raise your level of suspicion that there were perhaps other additions or add-ons made to these 10 entries that you evaluated in the notebook?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: That raised my suspicions because of the handwriting. In this case the handwriting didn't appear to be by somebody else. Therefore, no, it didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, if we look at the page to the right of this page which has the ERN number 0293-5753; do you have that?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Would you be kind enough just to move it over to your left so we could --

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sorry. Now, according to your report of the 16th of July, 2003, the first four lines of this page you attribute to Mr. Jokic. The balance or the rest of this page starting with the date and everything below the date you do not attribute to him; correct?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You seem to be hesitating.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Only because I was told to go up to that date.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And why is that?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Those were my instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: But did you ask for any reasons or the basis for those instructions?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to just ask a couple of questions on your other report that I found interesting. Just bear with me so I can find it. Do you remember if the letter "H" was not a match in your comparisons of Mr. Jokic's writing?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, how about we turn to the August 22nd, '03 report. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I should direct your attention to page 2, and that would be paragraph 4 of that report. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you find that the "H" was not well matched as well?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: I clearly found that it was not so well matched as some of the other characters.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: But you would agree with me and I think I've read some of your articles actually, you always say that the "H" is not well matched, don't you? I mean, even in your article you find that as a common non-match, if you will.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Not that I'm aware of.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We'll get to your article in a little bit. Let's stay with this paragraph 4. And you state there that there are a few characters that are not so well matched. For example, the "A", the "H", and the relative proportion of dots with circular diacritics. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You only give two examples there, but I'd like to know what other characters are not so well matched.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Again, off the top of my head I couldn't tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: But it's in your folder and file; correct?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. We'll get through some of it and then if the Court permits we'll take a look at your folder to get your complete testimony here.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: You continue on page 2 of this report of the 22nd of August, 2003, paragraph 4, to state the following: "In general, there are more diacritics in the questioned writings than in the specimen writings."

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. That's not true, is it?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: In what way?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, because there are not more diacritics, there are no diacritics in the specimen writing and that the only diacritics you found were in the questioned writing. So you seem to give us a kind of relative opinion there, but in fact as you earlier testified, in none of Mr. Jokic's documents or samplings, if you will, that you reviewed did you find a diacritic; correct?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: I didn't find the circular -- the large circular dot over the "I" but there were still additional marks to the characters.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I thought when we talked about diacritics that you said that's what it was, that it was the "I" --

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I mean the circle over the "I" and then we added the "J" for practical purposes, and I just want to focus on that and your testimony earlier today. Is this statement that in general there are more diacritics in the questioned writing than in the specimen writings?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Where in the specimen writing did you find a diacritic which was above the "I" or above the "J"?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: I was talking -- sorry, I may have misled you. For example, the additional what I would call accents that I pointed out on the "B".

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you consider an accent to be a diacritic?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: The diacritic is a mark above a letter. That's the term -- that's the way I was using it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: But I'm still correct, though, that if we -- let me just rephrase that. Sorry. Nowhere in Mr. Jokic's sampling did you find a diacritic of a circle over the letter "I" or the letter "J"; correct?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Again, I would have to refer to my notes to say nowhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to your next report. I have a couple questions on that. And that's the report of the 27th of January, 2004; correct?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just so we're on the same page. I get the impression when I read your three reports, ma'am, that you were asked by the Prosecution to elevate or to try to see if you can elevate your opinion from second to the top to the top. Would you agree with me on that? And that's why they asked you to look further into other documents and to examine other samplings and to give additional opinion, and you, as the professional as you are, refused and stuck with your opinion that that which was -- which it was, which was the second level as opposed to the top tier of your reasoned opinions; correct?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: I can't express an opinion on what their desire was.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, why didn't they, if you know, ask you to do further reports on the other three individuals whose handwriting you evaluated?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, looking at this 27th of January, 2000, report, I have a couple of questions and if I can direct your attention to page 2, and again it's paragraph 2.4. I'm sorry. The first sentence there you say: "There are some features of the --" and I'm just leading you to it. I think you can see it. I'm not trying to take it out of context, but you talk about similarities and then you talk about differences. You say there are some features of the questioned writings that cannot be matched in the specimens. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What are those?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Again, I go on to clarify that in my second -- in the sentence that follows.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yeah, but do you really clarify it or do you just regurgitate or restate what you said in your article, in your prior reports?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: In that sentence I'm merely repeating what I said in my prior report, to put into context, put it into context.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, if I can direct your attention to the next paragraph which is 2.5 of page 2 of your 27th January 2004 report. You talk about the additional handwriting sample that you received. Can you tell me what that was?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: That was what we referred to before, the sample handwriting that was produced by Mr. Jokic on request.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And that was where he actually reproduced all 10 pages of the notebook in which you were evaluating; correct?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The second sentence there you state that "there remained some features that differ between the specimen and the questioned writing." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Third line and fourth line of paragraph 2.5. What are those differences?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Again, it's the additional marks to the characters.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The diacritics?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: The diacritics, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You don't want to call them that any more?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How about the accents?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel and witness please make pauses between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I did hear it. Thank you. I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, what is -- you talked a little bit about fluency in your direct examination, and what is rarity? Do you know what rarity is?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: A criteria known as a rarity value?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: It's not a phrase that I've heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you -- what would you call it, a valuation? How often a letter or word comes up, did you do any evaluation based on that?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: How often the letter comes up or how often the construction of that letter comes up?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Probably the latter.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: So an evaluation, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, did you -- and in your notes do you reflect the number of times certain letters appeared and how you evaluated them, from this 10 pages of the notebook?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: I would reflect the different constructions of the characters, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And would you look at the quality of those characters?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: What do you mean by "quality"?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, if they were written with a more depressed manner as opposed to a light writing?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: That would be part of the fluency.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. So what is the criteria other than fluency, if you're not familiar with the rarity value? What is the criteria that you would utilise in addition to fluency to make your evaluation?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: To make my evaluation of what?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Of the task that you were given to determine whether a handwriting -- questioned handwriting sample is that of a specific individual or not.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: I would determine the construction of the characters, how they've been constructed by the pen movement and then additional features like the fluency, the slant, how they connect from one to the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Anything else?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Those would be the main ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, isn't all this that you talked about construction, pen movement, I think you mentioned basically the same, fluidity, the slant, et cetera, isn't that all that goes into your initial step, which we identify generally as the analysis of the handwriting specimen?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Was there another step process that you would do which is comparison of the observed handwriting characteristics?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: You would do the same -- the same bit that you just described for both sets of handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And then is there another step after that?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Then you would determine whether you considered that they were similar or different.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Which is normally in your profession called the assessment of the similarities and differences; right?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: That's one way of describing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. And how would you describe it?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: That's what I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. That's fair enough. And then do you also in your notebook have that as one of your tick sheets or in your notes that you actually analysed and made an assessment of the similarities and difference and that you actually observed or considered the comparisons of the handwriting characters? Is that broken down in your notes?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: To some extent.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And then finally I think in your process, the fourth step would be drawing a conclusion; correct?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, talking or getting back a little bit about this independent quality assurance or review, what material would these two individuals, although separate, looking at different reports, did they look at when they gave their peer review for your reports?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: The same documents that I looked at.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did they look at your notes?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: I would imagine --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The counsel and the witness will have to make pauses between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I know. And I apologise again, Your Honour. I will really make an effort to go slower.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please appreciate that --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- everybody's job in this courtroom is difficult but that of interpreters is particularly difficult. So please show some understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We have used this before. Perhaps this applies to both of you, Dr. Barr and Mr. Ostojic, wait until you see the scrolling of the transcript finished before you put your question or give your answer. I think that usually helps a lot. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may proceed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. By all means, slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I started to ask you, ma'am, if they looked, meaning the peer review persons that you identified whether they looked at your notes and you were starting to give us an answer.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: They would have my notes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What else, if anything, would they have other than your notes?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: They would have my notes and the writing that I'd looked at.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Anything else?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Not that I'm aware of.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, what about your report? Do you think they would need that if they would have to evaluate whether or not what you're purporting to be an opinion, whether that would be something that they can rely on and accept?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Sorry, I misunderstood. I was taking -- yes, obviously they would have my report. I was taking that as being part of my notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Anything else? You might have to answer out loud for the record?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Sorry. Not that I'm aware of.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Would they share their opinion with you in writing or verbally?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: A mix of both.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you have their written evaluation or assessment of your analysis for Mr. Jokic?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: If they wrote something down I would have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And it would be in your file?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We're still going too fast, I think. I'd like to direct your attention back to the 16th of July, 2003 report, page 4, if you will. And let me know when you ... And I know we covered it a little bit. I'm just not sure if I understand that paragraph in full. And just if I may read it because I'm not sure if everyone has it, with the Court's permission. 5.4 states as follows: "I would add that because of the nature of the entries, to which writings may have been added at a later date, if any small amount of writing was taken in isolation then the strength of evidence linking it to Dragan Jokic would, necessarily, be reduced." And I don't want to repeat the same question, ma'am, but I still don't understand what that paragraph means. What's it supposed to be telling us?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: It's supposed to be saying -- if I could use the book it would be easier to demonstrate rather than say in words.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It's not my book and the Court has suggested that we just be very careful because it's an original, so I don't know what you're going to do.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Just to have it up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't take what Dr. Barr has just stated to be that she would be marking the book. She will just be using the book to indicate what she needs to tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If the Court permits, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's fine. I think what I was trying to explain was that for example here we have an entry here, an entry here, and an entry here. It looks to be the same handwriting, and it looks to be the same ink, but I can't say whether they were done at one time or on three separate occasions and what time differences. So what I was trying to say was if, for example, you just took that line, then obviously there are only eight or nine characters in there, and therefore there is much less writing available for comparison than if you look at the writing in its totality.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. I'll review that and see if I understand it somewhat better. Did you ever conduct any microcharacteristics analysis of the writings in this notebook by Mr. Jokic?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Again, could you clarify what you mean by "microcharacteristic analysis".

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, you just now seem to evaluate and give an opinion and within seconds you felt that it was the same ink and the same writing. Do you agree with me that that analysis that you just offered is really woefully inadequate without using, at the very least, a microscope in order to determine whether or not the characteristics or the characters of various letters would or would not be considered a match?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Yes. I was using that for illustrative purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. I just didn't want --

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: -- anybody to misunderstand?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I think I understood you. Thank you. Now, you discussed briefly a range of variation in your direct examination. Could you share with me what was the range of variation in Mr. Jokic's writing from the questioned documents and the specimen document or writings?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: It would be the range of variation of the characters of each individual character. So I -- again that's part of my examination notes. There are a range of variation. In effect, we've seen it ourselves. When you pointed out the Bs on the previous page, each one is slightly different to the other. That is the range of variation that I'm talking about. Obviously, looking at more than just the ones on that page.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: With all due respect, I don't think that we covered all the Bs that I would like to cover with you.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: But with the example that I gave you, those two and then the third one added, I may disagree with your opinion, but I look forward to reading your notes on that. Can you tell us what the spectrum is when you talk about range of variation, like what is the two end points that you utilise in order to determine what that range was between the questioned writing on the specimen writing?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: There is no spectrum. I'm merely assessing how a person varies their writing.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, what's the level that you would use to determine if the range was wide or narrow?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: That would be my experience.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: There's no terminology that you can utilise to say that something is outside the range or within a range of variation?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: I would say something was outside the range of variation if it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And do you know if from document examiner to document examiner, since you say it's based on their opinion, that these ranges of variation can differ quite significantly?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: The ranges of variation aren't to do with the document examiner. They're to do with the writing.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, who evaluates the writing?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: The document examiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And who analyses the writing?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: The document examiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And one of the features and criteria for you to ultimately draw conclusion, you would examine the range of variation from the questioned writing and the specimen writing, would you not?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: I would, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. So would it vary, this range of variation from document examiner to document examiner when they make their analysis?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: They may think that certain characters are more variable than others.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So are you telling me that there's no standard range of variation, that's widely accepted whether in your country, the United Kingdom, or in Europe?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: I think we're mixing up terminologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What terminology, range or variation are we mixing up?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Range of variation reflects an individual person's writing so that would be the range of variation for that individual piece of writing. So it can't be standard across Europe or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: But when you make that assessment for that person's range of variation, my question is can it differ from document examiner to document examiner? One might consider it to be significant. Another examiner may consider it to be less significant, and a third one perhaps even insignificant. Would I be correct?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: That would be the comparison of the ranges of variation, not the ranges of variations themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And that analysis is also found hopefully in your notes; correct?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Yes. Whether it's -- again, it's a personal thing, so I would have what I consider to be my range of variation, but the range of variation, as I say, is sort of inherent in the writing. So it's the evaluation, I think, of the ranges of variation that I think you're saying are they standard.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I think I understand now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would request that we have or we get a copy of Dr. Barr's notebook, unless she objects of course, and I don't see why that wasn't produced to us, as we initially stated to the Court, this morning. We were told after 8:30 on Friday that she would be a witness given her schedule, but given that we don't have any of the bases for some of these opinions that we believe is necessary for further examination, we request a break at this point and to obtain a copy of those or the originals of her notebook so that we could examine it here today. And I find it odd that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: As I understand it, I don't believe that these were in the possession of the Prosecution. They were in the possession of the witness herself. So that's how I -- that's how I understand it. And having been a Judge in my life for so many years, that's how it's always been.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm not accusing them of anything, but I think they gave us two copies this morning of some of the things that she highlighted and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You had an explanation of that. I think it's fair enough that these notes be made available. I don't suppose you have any objection yourself, Dr. Barr. The question is -- I was going to ask you myself as you were approaching -- when you were approaching the end of your cross-examination actually whether it was your intention to recall at some point -- not recall, to put further questions later on to the witness after having had the opportunity to see these notes. So the question is whether -- we can always have a break now. That's no problem. It's only 10, 12 minutes before it's scheduled in any case. The question is I suppose your colleagues would be able to have of a look at these notes too. Second thing is custody of these notes, and third, how much time is needed, I because I wouldn't like to have a ping-pong game going on. I don't wish to have the same position arising when we deal with the cross-examination by the other lawyers.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: To answer your question, if I may, on some of them, it's difficult to assess until we see the extent of the notes. I don't have an appreciation for how detailed or how many there are. With the chain of custody, I think that obviously the Prosecution can be present or they can just photocopy if it's not too much trouble, or we can go with them and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What volume are we talking about, Dr. Barr?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A considerable volume.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: A considerable volume. I would have imagined so.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And just so the record's clear --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment because I need to consult with my colleagues of course. I've been dealing with it almost on a personal basis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's try to approach it in the most practical way that we can think of. We'll start a 30-minute break now. In the meantime, I would suggest that immediately after we leave the courtroom you have mutual consultations in which Dr. Barr has obviously to be included, for the availability of these documents. Do you have them here in the building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So that makes things easier. And then more or less how much time is required. We will reconvene in 30 minutes' time. Then you will enlighten us on -- you will come back to us with this information, and we'll decide accordingly. Thanks. Thirty minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. What are the good tidings, Mr. Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. President, and Your Honours. We've had an opportunity, and we to thank Dr. Barr for sharing with us during the break her notebook, and she actually highlighted or showed us what each thing generally meant, the general areas with the Prosecution obviously being present, and I think although I'm not a hundred per cent certain that although we initially thought Dr. Barr had scheduling problems, they are not problems presently and she is available to come back tomorrow. There are in fact two separate notebooks, one larger than the other. We didn't count the pages, but there's quite a significant if not overstated a substantial amount of material including her tick sheet and some personal handwritten notes that we think is important, at least for my client, because it highlights where we'd like to establish some differences in various letters in the word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So we've proposed, in essence, that we can continue asking for -- to the extent that the court allows us to come back tomorrow, and then I think my learned colleague, Mr. Bourgon, is going to ask about 20 minutes, if I can have 15 or 20 minutes to ask -- Bourgon, I listen to Mr. Meek to too often. So I think I have about 15, 20 minutes. I just want to finish what I thought I had prepared and then come back to it tomorrow with your leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Ostojic. Who else will be cross-examining Dr. Barr apart from Mr. Bourgon? No one else? No one else. Okay. Go ahead, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Doctor, once again thank you very much for accommodating us during the break and making your notes available. We appreciate it. I'd like to ask you in the -- with respect to the three Jokic reports that you created and tendered, did you at any point set out the letters or characters that you deemed to be similar as opposed to those we discussed to be different?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: In my notes, yes, there would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: But how about in your report?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Yes. In the second report I gave some examples.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And that's the 22nd of August report?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: It is, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. And that's on page 2, being correct?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now I know that it's not an exhaustive list, but nowhere in this sampling that you give us do you have the letter "B" either in upper or lowercase; correct?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Nowhere in this sampling --

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: I do have the "B" lowercase, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Nowhere -- and I have it highlighted. Nowhere in this sampling do you have a lower or uppercase E; correct? And this would be a sampling of similarities, just so that we're on the same page; correct?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Nowhere in your examples or samplings for similarities do you have an uppercase A; correct?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And nowhere in your examples or sampling do you have an upper or lowercase R; correct?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, do you know, although I know we're going to get your notes, but if you know off the top of your head having done three reports, do you know if you found those characters to be similar or as -- or different?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: As you say, without my notes --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: -- it would be difficult. I do know that with the "A" that in the original handwriting I had he tended to do a more angular -- with the two strokes were separate.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And we're talking about -- sorry to interrupt --

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Sorry. The uppercase "A". Where -- whereas -- that was in the questioned writings. In the specimens it tended mean more joined up, and I know I was able to match that feature better when I got the additional handwriting from him.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to see if you have in front of you his application, which is a document that was dated the 15th of August, 2001, and that is from Dragan Jokic. Do you have that with you perhaps?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: No, not here.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you utilise that to evaluate whether there were similarities or differences in the letters, upper and lowercase, of "B", "E", "A", "R", for example?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: I would need to see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. If I can -- with the Court's permission, it's ERN 02096264. And with the Court's permission, if the usher would be kind enough to just show it to Dr. Barr. The only problem is that I highlighted some of it so she should show it to the Prosecutor first, and then if it's okay with them. And, Dr. Barr, directing your attention to the ELMO, this is the "Zapisni" [phoen], as they call it of Dragan Jokic; correct?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you utilise his writing style from this form that happened to be in your file that was produced to us by the Office of the Prosecutor a couple of weeks ago?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you note anywhere there any of this diacritic that you were talking about with respect to specifically the "J" and the "I", where there would be a circle above it?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: No, there's not.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you notice anywhere there this accent or as we've discussed this embellishment you noted earlier or accent that can also be called a diacritic on the form?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: No, there's not.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Would that be indicative of anything, to say where you see an I with a diacritic such as a circle over it or a "J", that it would be dissimilar or different and therefore not the handwriting of Dragan Jokic whereas, as he writes in his application, he clearly, at least in this form, doesn't use the diacritic with the circle over the "I" or the "J" or any other accent for that matter?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Sorry, what was the question to start off?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Is that indicative of anything?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: It is a difference that I have taken into account in expressing a lower level of opinion, strong evidence rather than the conclusive evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And that would be the extent of it?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, going back, if you will, to the notebook, 377. Yes, it's right there. I'd like to ask you whether, when you reviewed the 10 pages given to the Prosecutor, whether you reviewed the originals or copies.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: I think originals.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. So how did you get the originals? Was it this complete green notebook that you have before you?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Sorry, when you say the originals, did you mean the originals in this notebook or the original sample handwriting from Mr. Jokic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about the notebook first.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's okay. And then we'll talk about his handwriting?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: I received the original of the notebook.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you go through the notebook for other pages other than those 10 pages that you were instructed to examine?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Since you had the notebook available to you? Sorry.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: I may -- I mean, obviously I looked through it, but I only concentrated on the pages that I was asked to look at.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So you don't know if Mr. Jokic made any other entries in this notebook because you haven't done any analysis or evaluation but for those 10 pages; correct?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, in your opinion would you agree that the more samples of writings or characters that you would -- characters that you would examine from an individual, the more reasonable you can make an opinion?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. So if you'd had 20 pages your opinion may have been enhanced or you may, in the alternative, altered your opinion to a lower standard or level of confidence. Would that be true?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: I may have done, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, looking in the book, it's not that significant or exhaustive, is it?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: The whole book?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yeah?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: For other examples of his writing?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: There would be a substantial amount of work involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know how many pages are in the book roughly?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Given that your opinion is the more samples we can have the stronger our opinion may become in terms of the weight that we can attribute to it, would it be unreasonable to have a handwriting expert examine 50 pages of documents?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What level would be unreasonable if we wanted to strengthen the weight that the opinion we're trying to derive from an expert?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: No amount would be unreasonable.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And no amount would be unreasonable if, specifically, it was a criminal trial would you agree with me on that?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Because the stakes are higher as opposed to a civil action?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: That's not really for me to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to direct your attention, if I may, to 0293-5748. Did you find it?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Is that within the group of documents that you reviewed from this notebook?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, just looking at this and I know you -- and we have your report on that, is -- can you tell from this writing if there was more than one person who wrote on this page 5748? And honestly, if you can't give us an opinion that would be fair. I don't mean to put you on the spot.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Well, from my reports, yes, there would be two writers.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And can you distinguish where these two writings would appear, below or above a certain line?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Yeah, below including that line.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. We don't see the full -- there we go. So everything below the first quarter starting with the letter "S", or the word that starts with the letter "S"; correct?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And above that is someone else, or is above that line Mr. Jokic?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Above that line is someone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, you've also done the evaluation, handwriting evaluation, for other duty officers at the Zvornik Brigade, Trbic and Mr. Drago Nikolic and the other guy, Strbac. I think he was mentioned. Did you conclude whose handwriting that was of those four? I think if you look at your report you'll find that neither of those three, at least in your opinion, made that entry, to be fair or to try to summarise it.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: But you're welcome to look at it if you don't take my word for it.

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: I'm sure you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, do you know who wrote it?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know when it was written?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know if it was something that was added at the top of the page at a later date?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you do any evaluation or analysis to determine any of those questions in conducting your review and analysis of these 10 pages from the notebook?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN JEAN BARR
utterances.text: As I've said before, assuming that I've said it's not any of those four, I would have done the handwriting bit. The bit as to when it was added, as I say, it's -- from just looking at the inks it would not be possible to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me within these 10 pages how many different purported writers there were for the contents of the material?
